questions.question: Which of the following pairs of structures are present in animal cells?
questions.explanation: Animal cells contain vacuoles (small) and a nucleus, but lack chloroplasts and cell walls which are found only in plant cells.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of elements is in the same period in the periodic table?
questions.explanation: Beryllium (atomic number 4) and Boron (atomic number 5) are both in Period 2 of the periodic table.

questions.question: The two main particles in the nucleus of an atom are
questions.explanation: The nucleus of an atom contains neutrons and protons. Electrons orbit outside the nucleus in energy shells.

questions.question: The current in a resistor is 3 A. If the resistance of the resistor is 4 ohms, determine the potential difference across the resistor.
questions.explanation: Using Ohm's law, V = IR = 3 A × 4 Ω = 12.00 V.

questions.question: The SI unit that is derived is
questions.explanation: The Pascal (Pa) is a derived SI unit for pressure, obtained from kg⋅m⁻¹⋅s⁻². The others (second, kelvin, kilogram) are base units.

questions.question: An example of a natural source of light is
questions.explanation: A glow worm produces its own light bioluminescence. The moon only reflects sunlight and is not a light source. Torchlight and lantern are artificial.

questions.question: An example of a mixture is
questions.explanation: Salt solution is a mixture of salt dissolved in water. The other options are all pure chemical compounds.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about acids are correct? I. They turn red litmus paper blue. II. They can be neutralized by bases. III. Citrus fruits contain acids.
questions.explanation: Statement I is false because acids turn blue litmus paper red, not the other way round. Statements II and III are correct.

questions.question: The farming system that makes the most effective use of land is
questions.explanation: Mixed cropping involves growing two or more crops on the same piece of land at the same time, making the most effective use of available land.

questions.question: The brightest of all the planets is
questions.explanation: Venus is the brightest planet in the sky as seen from Earth due to its highly reflective cloud cover and proximity to Earth.

questions.question: Artificial satellites can be used for I. communication. II. oil and gas exploration. III. meteorological studies.
questions.explanation: Artificial satellites are used for communication, oil and gas exploration (remote sensing), and meteorological (weather) studies.

questions.question: Which of the following electronic components is not made of semi-conductors?
questions.explanation: Capacitors are made of conductors and insulators (dielectrics), not semiconductors. Transistors, diodes, and LEDs are all semiconductor devices.

questions.question: Anemometer is an instrument for measuring
questions.explanation: An anemometer is a meteorological instrument used to measure wind speed.

questions.question: The following effects are as a result of soil erosion except
options: A. weakening of support of buildings.
D. loss of important minerals to plants.
questions.explanation: Soil erosion does not cause an increase in bushfires. It causes weakening of building support, weakening of plant support, and loss of minerals.

questions.question: Stirring of soil on vegetable beds is to I. improve aeration of soil. II. increase activities of soil organisms. III. increase water penetration in the soil. IV. reduce weed growth.
options: A. I, II and IV only
B. I, III and IV only
D. II, III and IV only
questions.explanation: Stirring improves aeration, increases water penetration by breaking surface crust, and reduces weed growth by disturbing young weeds.

questions.question: A pupil of mass 70 kg climbed a building of height 15 m. Determine the pupil's potential energy at the top of the building. [g = 10 m s⁻²]
questions.explanation: Potential energy = mgh = 70 × 10 × 15 = 10,500 J.

questions.question: Which of the following factors has the greatest influence on vegetable crop production?
questions.explanation: Water availability is the most critical factor influencing vegetable crop production since vegetables require regular watering.

questions.question: The grouping together of many stars is known as
questions.explanation: A galaxy is a massive system of stars, stellar remnants, interstellar gas, dust, and dark matter bound together by gravity.

questions.question: The following practices are cultural practices in crop production except
questions.explanation: Nursing (raising seedlings in a nursery) is done before transplanting to the field and is not classified as a cultural practice in crop production.

questions.question: The practice of reducing the number of seedlings per stand for better growth is known as
questions.explanation: Thinning out is the removal of excess seedlings from a stand to allow remaining ones enough space for better growth.

questions.question: The image formed by a plane mirror is always
questions.explanation: A plane mirror always forms a virtual, upright, and laterally inverted image of the same size as the object.

questions.question: The element used in the manufacturing of electronic components is
questions.explanation: Silicon is a semiconductor and is the most widely used element in the manufacture of electronic components such as transistors and diodes.

questions.question: Which of the following ions is formed by the loss of 2 electrons?
questions.explanation: Calcium (Ca²⁺) has lost 2 electrons, giving it a 2+ charge. Losing electrons forms positively charged ions (cations).

questions.question: The use of separating funnel is most appropriate for separating which of the following mixtures?
questions.explanation: A separating funnel is used to separate immiscible liquids. Water and vegetable oil do not mix and form distinct layers.

questions.question: The following products, X, Y, Z and W have masses 0.05 kg, 50 mg, 500 g and 0.05 g respectively. Which of the products have the same mass?
questions.explanation: Converting to grams: X = 50 g, Y = 0.05 g, Z = 500 g, W = 0.05 g. Y and W both have a mass of 0.05 g.

questions.question: If all the products (X, Y, Z and W) have equal volumes, which of the product(s) would have the highest density?
questions.explanation: Density = mass/volume. With equal volumes, the product with the highest mass (Z at 500 g) has the highest density.

questions.question: When equal amount of water is poured on dry soil samples, the increase in weight per unit amount of soil would be highest in
questions.explanation: Clayey soil has the highest water-holding capacity, so it absorbs the most water and shows the greatest weight increase.

questions.question: How many atoms are present in H₂O₂?
questions.explanation: H₂O₂ contains 2 hydrogen atoms and 2 oxygen atoms, making a total of 4 atoms.

questions.question: Which of the following body shapes facilitates movement in a fluid?
questions.explanation: A streamlined body shape reduces drag and facilitates easy movement through fluids like air or water.

questions.question: Steam changes to liquid by a process called
questions.explanation: Condensation is the process by which a gas (steam) changes into a liquid when it loses heat.

questions.question: Contour ploughing is normally practiced on
questions.explanation: Contour ploughing is done along the contour lines of sloping land to reduce soil erosion by slowing down water runoff.

questions.question: Which of the following statements distinguishes arteries from veins?
options: A. Arteries have relatively narrow lumen while veins have relatively wide lumen.
B. Arteries carry deoxygenated blood while veins carry oxygenated blood.
C. Arteries have valves while veins do not have valves.
D. Arteries transport blood to the heart while veins carry blood away from the heart.
questions.explanation: Arteries have thicker, more muscular walls with narrower lumens, while veins have thinner walls with wider lumens and contain valves.

questions.question: The base of the N-P-N transistor normally
options: A. is a p-type semi conductor.
B. is an n-type semi conductor.
D. have electrons as majority charge carriers.
questions.explanation: In an N-P-N transistor, the base is the middle layer made of p-type semiconductor material.

questions.question: The very hard greenish-black deposit around the corners of the teeth is known as
questions.explanation: Plaque is a hard deposit of bacteria, food debris, and minerals that forms on teeth, especially around the gum line.

questions.question: The daily variation of atmospheric conditions is called
questions.explanation: Weather refers to the short-term, daily changes in atmospheric conditions such as temperature, humidity, and rainfall.

questions.question: A herbal mixture has a volume of 200 m³ and a mass of 10,000 kg. Determine the density of the mixture.
questions.explanation: Density = mass/volume = 10,000/200 = 50 kg m⁻³.

questions.question: When a ray of light travels from a dense medium into a denser medium, it
options: A. is parallel to the incident ray.
B. bends away from the normal.
D. is perpendicular to the incident ray.
questions.explanation: When light passes from a less dense to a denser medium, it slows down and bends towards the normal line.

questions.question: To test for starch in a green leaf, it is usually boiled to
questions.explanation: Boiling a green leaf in alcohol extracts the green chlorophyll pigment, making it easier to observe the color change when iodine solution is added to test for starch.

questions.question: One benefit of technology to industrialization is
options: B. increase in cost of production.
questions.explanation: Technology provides machinery and tools that improve industrial processes and increase production efficiency.

questions.question: The following practices are principles in crop production except
questions.explanation: Land selection is a preparatory activity done before crop production begins, not a principle of crop production itself.

questions.question: Digestion of proteins starts from the
questions.explanation: Protein digestion begins in the stomach where the enzyme pepsin breaks down proteins into smaller peptides.

questions.question: A reflex action involves the
questions.explanation: A reflex action is an automatic response that involves the spinal cord and nerves, bypassing the brain for faster reaction.

questions.question: Which of the following structures is not part of the central nervous system?
questions.explanation: The central nervous system consists of the brain and spinal cord. Nerves are part of the peripheral nervous system, and veins are blood vessels.

questions.question: When the testa of a soaked bean is removed, the seed is seen to be made up of
questions.explanation: When the seed coat (testa) of a bean is removed, the two large cotyledons that store food are visible.

questions.question: One function of the root system of plants is to
options: C. hold the plant firmly in the ground
D. prepare food for the plant
questions.explanation: The root system anchors the plant firmly in the ground and absorbs water and minerals from the soil.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is caused by a virus?
questions.explanation: Cerebro-Spinal Meningitis (CSM) can be caused by viruses. Cholera is bacterial, malaria is parasitic, and TB is bacterial.

questions.question: The different types of teeth that an animal has gives an indication of the nature of its
questions.explanation: The types of teeth (incisors, canines, premolars, molars) reflect what and how an animal feeds.

questions.question: Exchange of gases takes place in the respiratory system through the
questions.explanation: Gas exchange between air and blood occurs in the lungs, specifically in the alveoli.

questions.question: Water that requires more soap in order to form lather is described as
questions.explanation: Hard water contains dissolved calcium and magnesium ions that react with soap, requiring more soap to form lather.

questions.question: One best way of making water safe for drinking is by
questions.explanation: Boiling kills disease-causing microorganisms in water, making it the most effective way to make water safe for drinking.

questions.question: The process whereby a hot saturated solution is cooled to obtain the solute is called
questions.explanation: Crystallization is the process of forming crystals by cooling a hot saturated solution, causing the dissolved solute to come out of solution.

questions.question: If a mixture of water and powdered charcoal is allowed to stand for a long time, the charcoal
options: C. dissolves completely in the water
D. continues to remain suspended in the water
questions.explanation: Charcoal is insoluble in water and, being denser than water, will settle at the bottom when the mixture is left to stand.

questions.question: The chemical symbol of potassium is
questions.explanation: Potassium has the chemical symbol K (from the Latin word Kalium). Na is sodium, Pb is lead, and S is sulphur.

questions.question: The atom of an element is represented as ¹⁷₃₅Cl. How many electrons are in the atom?
questions.explanation: In a neutral atom, the number of electrons equals the atomic number (proton number), which is the lower number 17.

questions.question: Which of the following agricultural practices prevents loss of water from the soil?
questions.explanation: Mulching involves covering the soil surface with organic material to reduce evaporation and conserve soil moisture.

questions.question: Soil conservation is important because it prevents loss of
questions.explanation: Soil conservation helps prevent the loss of essential minerals and nutrients from the soil through erosion and leaching.

questions.question: Foot rot disease in animals is caused by
questions.explanation: Foot rot in animals is primarily caused by fungi (and sometimes bacteria) that infect the foot tissues.

questions.question: A patient with symptoms of diarrhoea and vomiting may be suffering from
questions.explanation: Cholera is characterized by severe watery diarrhoea and vomiting, caused by the bacterium Vibrio cholerae.

questions.question: Which of the following human activities pollutes the environment? I. Release of cement dust into the atmosphere II. Dumping of refuse into water bodies III. Burning of rubbish
questions.explanation: All three activities — releasing cement dust, dumping refuse, and burning rubbish — pollute the environment.

questions.question: Which of the following features of a parent would not be inherited by the children?
questions.explanation: A scar is an acquired characteristic from injury and is not passed on genetically. Eye colour, nose shape, and height have genetic components.

questions.question: Which of the following bodies is at the centre of the solar system?
questions.explanation: The Sun is at the centre of the solar system, and all the planets, including Earth, orbit around it.

questions.question: The chemicals used in the preparation of ammonia in the laboratory are
options: A. ammonium chloride and calcium hydroxide
B. ammonium nitrate and sodium chloride
C. ammonium sulphate and calcium chloride
D. ammonium sulphate and sodium chloride
questions.explanation: Ammonia is prepared in the laboratory by heating a mixture of ammonium chloride and calcium hydroxide (slaked lime).

questions.question: Steel is an alloy of
questions.explanation: Steel is an alloy made primarily of iron with a small percentage of carbon, which gives it strength and hardness.

questions.question: The property of a metal that makes it possible for it to be beaten into different shapes is called
questions.explanation: Malleability is the property of a metal that allows it to be hammered or beaten into thin sheets or different shapes without breaking.

questions.question: Movement of the particles of a gas from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration is known as
questions.explanation: Diffusion is the movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration until evenly distributed.

questions.question: Oxygen in the blood finally reaches the parts of the body through the
questions.explanation: Capillaries are tiny blood vessels that reach into body tissues, allowing oxygen and nutrients to diffuse into cells.

questions.question: An aluminium cube with side measuring 2 m has a mass of 24 kg. Calculate the density of the aluminium.
questions.explanation: Volume = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 m³. Density = mass/volume = 24/8 = 3 kgm⁻³.

questions.question: The force that opposes the motion of an object on another object is called
questions.explanation: Frictional force is the force that opposes or resists the motion of an object moving over a surface.

questions.question: Water is prevented from passing through the tiny holes in an umbrella by
questions.explanation: Surface tension allows water to form a thin film over the tiny holes in umbrella fabric, preventing it from passing through.

questions.question: Which of the following methods of preserving food makes use of heat energy from the sun?
questions.explanation: Drying (sun-drying) uses heat energy from the sun to remove moisture from food, preventing bacterial growth and spoilage.

questions.question: The following factors hinder vegetable production in Ghana except
options: A. high cost of agricultural chemicals.
B. lack of market for farm produce.
questions.explanation: Availability of sunlight is beneficial for vegetable production, not a hindrance. The other options are challenges faced by vegetable farmers.

questions.question: The S.I unit of energy is represented as
questions.explanation: The SI unit of energy is the Joule, and its standard symbol is a capital J.

questions.question: A book is at rest on a table. The net force acting on the book could be described as one that
questions.explanation: When an object is at rest, the forces acting on it are balanced — the downward gravitational force equals the upward normal force from the table.

questions.question: An example of a communicable disease is
questions.explanation: Hepatitis (especially viral hepatitis) is communicable because it can be spread from person to person. Asthma, diabetes, and hypertension are non-communicable.

questions.question: To stop the spread of a disease caused by a dirty environment, one must
questions.explanation: Practicing personal hygiene, including keeping the environment clean, is the most effective way to prevent diseases caused by dirty environments.

questions.question: An animal feed made up of high fibre is most likely to contain
questions.explanation: Silage is fermented plant material (grass or other forage crops) that is high in fibre and commonly used as animal feed.

questions.question: Charles Darwin is famous for
options: B. his work on the origin of the universe.
C. his work in the field of physics.
D. his theory of natural selection.
questions.explanation: Charles Darwin is best known for his theory of evolution by natural selection, published in 'On the Origin of Species'.

questions.question: A mango of mass 2 kg hangs 15 m on top of a mango tree. Determine the value of the kinetic energy attained just before it hits the ground. [g = 10 m s⁻²]
questions.explanation: At the top, the mango has potential energy = mgh = 2 × 10 × 15 = 300 J. Just before hitting the ground, all this potential energy converts to kinetic energy = 300 J.

questions.question: Which of the following Ghanaian scientists is known for promoting Mathematics and Physics?
questions.explanation: Prof. Francis Allotey was a renowned Ghanaian physicist known for his work in mathematics and physics, particularly the Allotey formalism.

questions.question: An example of a mono-gastric animal is
questions.explanation: A rabbit is a monogastric animal with a single-chambered stomach. Cattle, goats, and sheep are ruminants with multi-chambered stomachs.

questions.question: Which of the following statements accurately explains the positions of calcium and magnesium in the periodic table? They all have the same
questions.explanation: Both calcium (2,8,8,2) and magnesium (2,8,2) have 2 valence electrons, placing them in the same group (Group 2) of the periodic table.

questions.question: Which of the following food substances would produce a red precipitate when heated with Millon's reagent?
questions.explanation: Millon's reagent tests for proteins (specifically the amino acid tyrosine). Groundnut is rich in protein and would produce a red precipitate.

questions.question: The rise in heat waves and floods globally may be due to the effect of
questions.explanation: Climate change, driven by increased greenhouse gas emissions, is causing more frequent and intense heat waves and floods worldwide.

questions.question: Which of the following waste disposal practices is best for plastic disposal?
questions.explanation: Recycling is the best method for disposing of plastic waste because it reuses the material and reduces environmental pollution.

questions.question: The first step in the digestion of fats in the body is that
options: A. bile breaks down the fat in the gall bladder.
B. bile breaks down the fat in the duodenum.
C. lipase breaks down the fat in the pancreas.
D. lipase breaks down the fat in the ileum.
questions.explanation: Bile is produced in the liver, stored in the gall bladder, and released into the duodenum where it emulsifies (breaks down) fats.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms is prokaryotic?
questions.explanation: Bacteria are prokaryotes, meaning they lack a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles. Earthworms, fungi, and plants are eukaryotes.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best explains animal feed?
options: A. Food grown or developed for livestock
B. Balanced diet provided to animals
C. Breast milk served to a calf
D. Grass that is used to feed livestock
questions.explanation: Animal feed is food grown or produced specifically for consumption by livestock, including grains, forages, and formulated mixes.

questions.question: Which of the following activities does not relate to the principles of pressure in the daily lives of humans?
options: A. Drinking straw in use by people at a party
B. Pumping air into car tyres
C. Filling of balloons with air
D. A person jerking forward when a speeding car suddenly stops
questions.explanation: A person jerking forward in a stopping car is due to inertia (Newton's first law), not pressure. The other options all involve atmospheric or gas pressure.

questions.question: A patient has been diagnosed with hypertension. Which of the following readings is most likely the patient's blood pressure?
questions.explanation: Hypertension is diagnosed when blood pressure is consistently 140/90 mmHg or higher. The other readings are within or near normal range.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases can be classified as a viral disease?
questions.explanation: H1N1 (swine flu) is caused by a specific type of influenza A virus. Candidiasis and ringworm are fungal, while most meningitis is bacterial.

questions.question: A grassland ecosystem that consists of snakes, toads and grasshoppers is most likely to produce a food chain of
questions.explanation: In a food chain, energy flows from producers to consumers: grass (producer) → grasshopper (primary consumer) → toad (secondary consumer) → snake (tertiary consumer).

questions.question: A fruit with sour taste is most likely to have a pH that is
questions.explanation: Sour-tasting fruits are acidic, and acidic substances have a pH value less than 7 on the pH scale.

questions.question: Which of the following associations between two organisms is always beneficial to both?
questions.explanation: Mutualism is a type of symbiotic relationship where both organisms benefit. Commensalism benefits only one organism.

questions.question: Which of the following substances are major components of human blood? I. Hormones II. Platelets III. Plasma IV. White blood cells
options: D. II, III and IV only
questions.explanation: The major components of blood are plasma, red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. Hormones are not a major structural component of blood.

questions.question: Combination of science, technology and innovation is needed in Ghana because it
options: A. equips students to travel abroad and work.
B. makes students develop interest in science, technology and innovation.
C. makes students understand their environment better.
questions.explanation: The combination of science, technology, and innovation drives industrialization and economic growth, thereby promoting national development.

questions.question: A rod appears bent when immersed in water. What property of light is demonstrated?
questions.explanation: Refraction is the bending of light as it passes from one medium to another (e.g., from water to air), causing objects to appear bent or displaced.

questions.question: Which of the following heart conditions in humans is caused by plaque deposits in the arteries?
questions.explanation: Atherosclerosis is the buildup of plaques (fats, cholesterol, and other substances) in and on the artery walls, narrowing the arteries.

questions.question: A breeding female pig is called a
questions.explanation: A sow is an adult female pig that has farrowed (given birth). A gilt is a young female pig that has not yet given birth.

questions.question: Which of the following energy sources is/are environmentally friendly? I. Wind II. Hydro III. Biomass
questions.explanation: Wind, hydro, and biomass are all renewable energy sources that are considered environmentally friendly compared to fossil fuels.

questions.question: Germs that infect the respiratory system are frequently spread through I. mucus II. air pollution III. coughs
questions.explanation: Respiratory germs can be spread through mucus droplets, polluted air, and coughing, all of which can transmit pathogens to others.

questions.question: The chemical formula of iron (II) sulphide is
questions.explanation: Iron (II) has a charge of +2 and sulphide has a charge of -2, so they combine in a 1:1 ratio to form FeS.

questions.question: The following soil qualities are important for crop production except
questions.explanation: High salinity (excess salt) is harmful to crops as it causes water stress and toxicity. Nutrient availability, oxygen, and water-holding capacity are all beneficial.

questions.question: The characteristics of a fertile soil include good I. aeration II. texture III. water-holding capacity
questions.explanation: Fertile soil has good aeration (air spaces), appropriate texture (balanced particle sizes), and good water-holding capacity to support crop growth.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best explains why gases are more compressible than solids?
options: A. Particles in gases are smaller than in solids
B. Gases have fixed volume but solids do not
C. Particles in solids have definite shape but gases have no definite shape
D. Particles in gases have wider intermolecular spaces as compared to solids
questions.explanation: Gas particles are far apart with large intermolecular spaces, allowing them to be compressed closer together. Solid particles are tightly packed.

questions.question: Which of the following substances has a definite shape?
questions.explanation: Stone is a solid and has a definite shape. Air is a gas, kerosene and water are liquids — none of these have a definite shape.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best explains livestock feed?
options: A. Food grown or developed for livestock
B. Balanced diet provided to animals
C. Breast milk served to a calf
D. Grass that is used to feed livestock
questions.explanation: Livestock feed broadly refers to any food grown, produced, or developed for feeding farm animals, including grains, forages, and concentrates.

questions.question: Charles Darwin is famous for
options: B. his work on the origin of the universe.
C. his work in the field of physics.
D. his theory of natural selection.
questions.explanation: Charles Darwin proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection, explaining how species evolve over time through survival of the fittest.

questions.question: Which of the following statements accurately explains the positions of calcium and magnesium in the periodic table? They all have the same
questions.explanation: Both calcium (Ca) and magnesium (Mg) are in Group 2 and each has 2 valence electrons in their outermost shell.

questions.question: An animal feed made up of high fibre is most likely to contain
questions.explanation: Silage is fermented forage material that is naturally high in fibre, making it a suitable feed for ruminant animals.

questions.question: The term used to describe a rabbit giving birth is
questions.explanation: Kindling is the term for when a rabbit gives birth to its young (kits). Culling means removing animals, and weaning is stopping milk feeding.

questions.question: Which of the following substances is a compound?
questions.explanation: Water (H₂O) is made of two different elements, hydrogen and oxygen, chemically combined.

questions.question: An atom of an element has a neutral charge because the
options: A. protons and electrons are the same particles
B. proton number and electron number are the same
C. neutron number and proton number are equal
D. electron number and neutron number are equal
questions.explanation: Equal numbers of positive protons and negative electrons make the atom electrically neutral.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms is an ecto-parasite of animals?
questions.explanation: Fleas live on the surface (skin) of the host, so they are ecto-parasites; the others live inside hosts (endo-parasites).

questions.question: An atom has 20 nucleons and 9 protons. What is its neutron number?
questions.explanation: Nucleons = protons + neutrons, so neutrons = 20 − 9 = 11.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about aerobic and anaerobic respiration is not correct?
options: A. Water is produced as a by-product in anaerobic respiration
B. Alcohol or lactic acid is produced in anaerobic respiration
C. No oxygen is required in anaerobic respiration
D. Very little energy is released in anaerobic respiration
questions.explanation: Water is a by-product of aerobic (not anaerobic) respiration, so statement A is incorrect.

questions.question: An aluminium cube of side 2 m has a mass of 24 kg. Determine the density of the aluminium.
questions.explanation: Volume = 2³ = 8 m³; density = 24 ÷ 8 = 3 kg m⁻³.

questions.question: What is the systematic name of the compound CO?
questions.explanation: CO (carbon monoxide) has carbon in the +2 oxidation state, so its systematic name is carbon (II) oxide.

questions.question: Which of the following methods can be used to prevent iron from rusting? I. Painting  II. Alloying  III. Keeping the iron in a desiccator  IV. Keeping iron in a moist environment
options: C. I, II and III only
D. II, III and IV only
questions.explanation: Painting, alloying and keeping iron dry all prevent rusting; a moist environment promotes it.

questions.question: The proper way of maintaining soil structure and fertility is termed as soil
questions.explanation: Soil conservation is the practice of maintaining soil structure and fertility.

questions.question: The instrument that can be used to measure accurately the mass of a substance is
questions.explanation: Mass is accurately measured with a beam balance; a spring balance measures weight.

questions.question: Which of the following chemical symbols can be used to remove permanent hardness of water?
questions.explanation: Sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃) reacts with the dissolved calcium/magnesium salts to remove permanent hardness.

questions.question: Which of the following chemical symbols is that of an element with seven electrons in the outermost shell?
questions.explanation: Chlorine's electronic configuration is 2,8,7, so its outermost shell has 7 electrons.

questions.question: Which of the following fruits is dispersed by water?
questions.explanation: Coconut has light, hollow, floating seeds that are dispersed by water.

questions.question: A farming system which involves the growing of rice and the rearing of fowls is known as
questions.explanation: Mixed farming is growing crops together with rearing livestock on the same farm.

questions.question: A machine lifts a load of 100 N through a vertical distance of 2 m in 10 s. What is the work done by the machine?
questions.explanation: Work = force × distance = 100 × 2 = 200 J.

questions.question: The energy transformation that takes place in a solar cell is
questions.explanation: A solar cell converts light energy directly into electrical energy.

questions.question: All flowering plants end their life cycle with
questions.explanation: The final stage in a flowering plant's life cycle is seed dispersal.

questions.question: Soil texture is a term used to describe the
options: A. amount of water soil can hold
B. arrangement of soil particles in a given soil
C. proportions of sand, silt and clay in a sample of soil
D. mixture of all soil particles
questions.explanation: Soil texture refers to the relative proportions of sand, silt and clay particles in the soil.

questions.question: Which of the following processes is an example of a physical change?
questions.explanation: Magnetizing iron is a temporary physical change; the chemical identity of the iron is unchanged.

questions.question: An example of a storage pest is
questions.explanation: Weevils are insects that damage stored grains and other stored food, so they are storage pests.

questions.question: The solid component found on the filter paper and the liquid component that flows into a container during filtration are respectively called
questions.explanation: The solid left on the filter paper is the residue; the liquid that passes through is the filtrate.

questions.question: A capacitor is connected in a series circuit with an LED, a battery and a switch. When the circuit is closed, the LED
options: A. comes on and stays on
questions.explanation: The LED lights briefly while the capacitor charges, then goes off once the capacitor is fully charged.

questions.question: The ion that causes hardness in water is
questions.explanation: Calcium (Ca²⁺) and magnesium (Mg²⁺) ions cause permanent hardness of water.

questions.question: Which of the following substances are matter? I. Hydrogen  II. Air  III. Stone
questions.explanation: Hydrogen, air and stone all have mass and occupy space, so all are matter.

questions.question: The main reason for staking tomato is to ensure
options: B. air circulation on the farm
C. upright growth of the plant
D. that fruits do not get rotten
questions.explanation: Staking supports the tomato plant to grow upright and keeps it off the ground.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about clayey soil is not true? It
options: A. swells when dry and shrinks when wet
C. is difficult to plough when dry

questions.question: Which of the following planets are closer to the sun than the Earth?
questions.explanation: Mercury and Venus lie between the Sun and the Earth (their orbits are closer to the Sun).

questions.question: What force makes a ripe mango fall from a tree?
questions.explanation: The mango falls because of the Earth's gravitational pull on it.

questions.question: Urea is a good source of
questions.explanation: Urea is a nitrogen-rich fertilizer that supplies nitrogen to the soil.

questions.question: Which of the following substances is a compound?
questions.explanation: Sucrose (C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁) is made of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen chemically combined; the others are elements.
